correctness.rationale: C PASS: For 1<p<infinity, p!=2, two independent Gaussian coordinates and rates alpha,beta>0, Janson's complex second-quantization criterion/Epperson's one-variable region gives boundedness iff |sin(alpha s)|<=k_p sinh(alpha t) and |sin(beta s)|<=k_p sinh(beta t), t>=0; coordinate restriction gives necessity and Fubini tensorization sufficiency including the boundary, operator norm exactly one from constants. The threshold h(s) is max of the two inverse-asinh sine heights. Imaginary periods must map zero to simultaneous sine zeros, hence exactly the common pi-lattice for rational beta/alpha and {0} otherwise. Kronecker equidistribution of irrational torus flow gives product normalized arcsine interval lengths, with quadratic small-t asymptotic. Coprime integer rates yield a unique shrinking common zero arc modulo pi/omega, producing first-order coefficient 2k_p omega/pi. For irrational theta, distance to the two zero lattices and midpoint choice make minimal max-distance half their separation; selecting nearest integer pairs along best approximations establishes liminf |s|h(s)=pi^2 lambda(theta)/(2k_p alpha beta). The liminf is not an all-s estimate; rational small-t errors are fixed-rate, not denominator-uniform. Independently checked several rational and irrational small-t constants numerically. Finite checks cannot replace the boundary theorem or equidistribution.
